text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 0.52% today to $422.33, continuing a sharp rally that started yesterday when the stock jumped nearly 7%. The jump appears tied to crude oil's strength — US oil closed near $96 per barrel today, and the gap between world oil prices ($113.96) and US prices has widened significantly, which typically improves refining margins. Refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, near full utilization, so they're positioned to capture those higher margins as crude stays elevated.

The broader backdrop has shifted toward tighter fuel supplies: the G7 announced it will release 100 million barrels of reserves over four months to combat high diesel prices, and geopolitical risks in the Middle East and Europe remain elevated. These supply constraints and the potential for continued disruptions have kept oil prices firm, which benefits refiners like Marathon that process crude into fuel.
